title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 80–82): this is Grothendieck's 'surgery of conformal surfaces', i.e. building a smooth Riemann surface X out of a nodal one. Start from X'', the disjoint union (normalisation) of the pieces X''' of a stable curve. X'' carries pairs of points (x'_i, x''_i) that are to be joined at nodes, plus marked points x_α. The gluing datum at the i-th node is a tensor u_i ∈ T*_{x'_i} ⊗ T*_{x''_i}, equivalently a pairing T_{x'_i} ⊗ T_{x''_i} → C. Choosing a round (conformal) disc D'_i in T_{x'_i} determines, through this pairing, a 'polar' disc D''_i in T_{x''_i}. Rescaling D'_i by λ rescales D''_i by 1/λ.

This page continues as follows.
1. Neighbourhoods of these discs are embedded in X'' via some local coordinates; the previous page suggests a canonical hyperbolic choice, e.g. cusp coordinates.
2. Their boundary circles are then related by orientation-reversing isomorphisms ('antiisos').
3. Removing the open discs and gluing the boundaries pairwise gives a Riemann surface X. If one also removes small discs D̊_α around the marked points, X is a surface with boundary; otherwise it is a surface with marked points.
4. X contains the image circles Γ_i. These are not hyperbolic geodesics in general, but each is freely homotopic to a unique simple closed geodesic ('principes de Thurston').
5. The result is therefore a point of Teichmüller/moduli space near the boundary stratum, together with a pants decomposition. In modern terms this is the plumbing construction z·w = t, with t essentially u_i, together with the passage to the associated hyperbolic pants decomposition. Its purpose is to define 'arrows in the reverse direction' between categories or fibrations attached to moduli of curves (previous page).

Grothendieck then asks whether the result is independent of the choice of the polar pair (D'_i, D''_i). He offers a heuristic: a small change λ near 1 changes X only by moving Γ_i to nearby curves Γ'_i. He calls this 'tout à fait vaseux', and the next page says 'probablement tout à fait faux'. He then singles out (g,ν) = (0,4) — two pants glued along one curve, with boundary lengths l_i and a twist θ — as the key case. That amounts to comparing plumbing data with Fenchel–Nielsen length/twist coordinates.
errors: The independence worry is partly misplaced. Once local coordinates at x'_i and x''_i are fixed, the gluing is the single relation z·w = t. Replacing the radius r by λr only changes which collar is used, so the glued surface X is literally the same. The Γ_i move within the same free homotopy class, so the associated geodesics are unchanged. The genuine gap lies elsewhere: X depends on the full coordinate germs, not just on the first-order datum u_i ∈ T*⊗T*. The construction is canonical only if one uses canonical coordinates, e.g. hyperbolic cusp/horocycle coordinates. The note does not settle which coordinates are meant.

ideas.what: Gluing a nodal surface along polar discs determined by a tensor in T*_{x'}⊗T*_{x''}
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing construction / smoothing of nodes (deformation parameter in T'⊗T'' = normal direction to a boundary divisor of M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kodaira–Spencer, Earle–Marden, Kra, Fay, Bers (1960s–70s); Wolpert, Masur
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) evokes the Teichmüller tower and gluing of pants, but not this construction explicitly

ideas.what: Curves Γ_i of the glued surface replaced by unique homotopic geodesics, giving a pants decomposition
Comparison of plumbing parameters with Fenchel–Nielsen (length, twist) data, the (0,4) case being key
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing vs Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates near the boundary of moduli space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wolpert (1990, 'The hyperbolic metric and the geometry of the universal curve', and later work)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard plumbing construction combined with Thurston-style geodesic straightening, aimed at relating plumbing data to length/twist data. It is interesting as a sign that Grothendieck worked concretely on the Teichmüller tower around 1983–84. However, the comparison of plumbing and Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates was carried out by Wolpert and others, and the page itself is tentative and self-doubting.
transcription_corrections: 'trouve des arêtes entre leurs bords' should probably read 'trouve des antiiso entre leurs bords' (orientation-reversing isomorphisms between the boundary circles)
'paires (D'_i, D''_i) mut. pleines' should probably read 'mut.t polaires' (mutually polar discs); likewise 'disque conforme plein' on the previous page is likely 'polaire'
'ne dépend pas des choix des paires' confirmed
